video_title: Cav’s Owner Dan Gilbert on LeBron, Billionaires, and Rebuilding a City

quotes.speaker: Dan Gilbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Gilbert on the Cavaliers' front-row seat policy
quotes.excerpt: we put in a policy that our front-row seats could not sell their seats
quotes.quote: What really happened was, it wasn't just him. We put in a policy that our front-row seats could not sell their seats. That was even from earlier in the season. Anybody who owns courtside seats for Cleveland Cavaliers games in Cleveland could not sell their seats to anyone else. And Fat Joe bought them, presumably on the market, and you denied him the seat?

text_blocks.speaker: Nayeema Raza
text_blocks.text: So, anybody who owns courtside seats for Cleveland Cavaliers games in Cleveland could not sell their seats to anyone else. And Fat Joe bought them, presumably on the market, and you denied him the seat?

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Gilbert
text_blocks.text: Well, I don't think we denied him. I think they probably weren't able to sell it to him.

quotes.speaker: Dan Gilbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Gilbert on the sale of Quick and Loans
quotes.excerpt: It was all stock for stock deal, but I think it turned out when you did the numbers
quotes.quote: It was all stock for stock deal, but I think it turned out when you did the numbers to be about 500 million. But then we bought it back two years later for a lot less, so that was good.

quotes.speaker: Dan Gilbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Gilbert explains the FAST acronym for stroke symptoms
quotes.excerpt: there's an acronym called FAST. Face, arms, speech, and time, meaning get your butt to the hospital
quotes.quote: There's an acronym called FAST. Face, arms, speech, and time, meaning get your butt to the hospital the first three hours. If their face starts drooping, if they hold their arms out and they start falling, and if their speech is hard, then you got to get to the hospital. Time, beat the clock.

quotes.speaker: Dan Gilbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Gilbert on the NBA's fair revenue sharing and ownership model
quotes.excerpt: It's great that the union and the owners have come to a agreed agreement over the last ten years.

text_blocks.speaker: Naeem
text_blocks.text: Do you think the NBA is the most fair thing in America?

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Gilbert
text_blocks.text: It's great that the union and the owners have come to a agreed agreement over the last ten years. It really allows the NBA to flourish. And they're checking on each other. It's almost like 50/50 of the revenue. Of course, the owners have all the costs.

quotes.speaker: Dan Gilbert

text_blocks.speaker: Naeem
text_blocks.text: So you like this idea of giving more money to taxpayers, having taxpayers participate more in wealth creation when the government is making subsidies?

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Gilbert
text_blocks.text: If the government's going to give a subsidy or something, why shouldn't they get equity? Yeah, why not?

text_blocks.text: What are the other things that the US could learn from this NBA model about being fair, about some level of redistribution? I mean, that's really what the NBA is doing, right? Redistributing talent so that the game is still worth watching.

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Gilbert
text_blocks.text: Keep in mind they're forced to do that because they're going to lose fans if you don't have a competitive league. But all the leagues do that. Baseball does that, football does that, hockey does that.

quotes.speaker: Dan Gilbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Gilbert on encouraging companies to take an activist role in local issues
quotes.excerpt: I'd like to encourage other companies to take an activist role in one big issue.
quotes.quote: I think from my standpoint, what we've done as a business, I'd like to encourage other companies to take an activist role in one big issue. Because when you're a company, you've got an army of people that are working in the business. We have 15,000 in Detroit, that's a lot of people. And all of them participate in something. So that's a lot of people to get a lot of things done. You have access to capital, you have relationships you built up over decades.

quotes.speaker: Dan Gilbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Gilbert on the 'more than profit' business philosophy
quotes.excerpt: We want to start calling our business a more than profit, which means yes, we care about profits, but we're doing more than that.
quotes.quote: We've come up with this concept, there's for-profit, there's not-for-profit, we want to start calling our business a more than profit, which means yes, we care about profits, but we're doing more than that.
